pr_title: BUG: Cast ExtensionArray to numpy ndarray before plot
pr_body:
Cast `ExtensionArray`(eg. `IntegerArray`) to `np.ndarray` before send to matplotlib to plot, fixes #25587.

- [x] closes #25587
- [x] tests added / passed
- [x] passes `git diff upstream/master -u -- "*.py" | flake8 --diff`
- [x] whatsnew entry

comments: it's pandas 0.24.1 with this commit applied on top https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/pull/25289. I haven't tried master but the bug should be valid for 0.24.1.

Thanks for the report. Let us know if you want to work on a fix for this. Something in matplotlib doesn't like extension arrays, which can't be reshaped to 2d arrays. We may need to convert before passing to mpl.

review_comments: will a plot actually work if there are nulls?

@jreback  do you mean there are `nan`s or `None`s in the integer_array? It will also can be plotted.

In fact, `np.asarray` will transform `None` as `np.nan`, and the result dataframe still can be plotted.

```
>>> a = integer_array([1,2,3,None], dtype="Int64")
>>> a
<IntegerArray>
[1, 2, 3, NaN]
Length: 4, dtype: Int64
>>> np.asarray(a)
array([1, 2, 3, nan], dtype=object)
```
I think you can just call ``np.asarray`` for  all columns
That doesn't work well. Tons of `SettingWithCopyError` would be raised when run `pandas/tests/plotting/test_frame.py`.

`.assign` still doesn't work (if I don‘’t miss something). `.assign` requires `kwargs`, which is a dict of `{str. callable or Series}`, however in many dataframes the column label may not be a string (like `pd.DataFrame([1,2,3])`).
